text:
samir: hey all — trying to get the local dev stack up. docker-compose brings up services but postgres exits immediately. error in logs: 'initdb: could not create directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata/pg_wal": Permission denied'. i'm on macbook air M2, Docker Desktop 4.26. also have a WireGuard VPN active. anyone seen this?
jen: yep seen that. usually when people bind-mount a host folder that has root-owned files. are you using a bind mount for ./pgdata?
samir: yes in compose i have 'volumes:
  - ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data'
leo: that will give the container the host's permissions. postgres image runs as uid 999. try chowning the host dir to 999:999 or switch to a named volume.
leo: e.g. on host:
```bash
sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata
docker-compose up
```
maya: alternative is to change compose to use a named volume so Docker manages ownership:
```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
volumes:
  pgdata:
    driver: local
```
jen: also note some VPNs / corporate network mounts (and macOS file sharing with certain file systems) can cause weird permission behavior. WireGuard itself usually ok, but if your pgdata is on a synced folder (iCloud/Dropbox) user IDs can mismatch.
infra-bot: FYI docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/dev/local-db-setup — prefer named volumes for most devs. :information_source:
samir: hm i'm not using iCloud or Dropbox. pgdata was created by sudo earlier when i tried a workaround. gonna chown then try named volume if that fails.
leo: if chown doesn't work, try removing the host bind and start with named volume then copy data in if you need it.
samir: quick question — is it safe to run chown 999:999 on my project folder?
jen: only chown the pgdata dir, not the whole repo. sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata is fine. also `ls -ln ./pgdata` will show numeric owner so you can confirm.
maya: if you still hit problems, paste the output of `docker-compose logs db` and we can take a look.
samir: did chown and restarted — postgres now runs! Thanks all :tada:
jen: :thumbsup: welcome aboard, and ping #eng-infra if you want us to add a quick note to the onboarding doc about WireGuard caveats.
samir: will do — thanks again!
